text: As global travel returns to pre-pandemic levels, the issue of overtourism is becoming a major concern again. With only 800 ____ (people who live in an area), Hallstatt receives around 10,000 tourists per day, leading to rising tensions.

Overtourism happens when too many visitors gather in one place, causing social, economic, and environmental problems. Landmarks and natural sites suffer from ____ (too much) crowds, pollution, and damage. In some areas, housing prices have risen as landlords prioritize short-term rentals over local residents. Long lines, high prices, and overcrowding make sightseeing less enjoyable for tourists as well.

Many residents in heavily visited locations are fighting back. Hallstatt locals staged a protest, while Venice ____ large cruise ships from its main canal. Other places, such as Orkney in Scotland and Kenya’s Maasai Mara, are also ____ (forcing into existence) new rules to manage visitor numbers.

Cities are introducing taxes and visitor limits. Venice plans to ____ (make someone pay) day-trippers a fee, and Amsterdam is banning cruise ships. Authorities are encouraging off-season travel and directing tourists to less-visited locations. Some experts suggest that local communities should have a say in how tourism is managed to balance economic ____ (advantages) with quality of life.

Despite the challenges, tourism remains a key part of the global economy. The industry is expected to reach pre-pandemic levels soon, and more travelers are considering tourism options. While there is no single solution to overtourism, better planning and responsible travel can help reduce its negative effects.
